In Figure 1 (page 6), **"GeM Pooling"** produces the aggregated history embedding from the visited-profile embeddings, and **"Temporal-Gated Pooling"** produces the aggregated user embedding (Step 1 of the diagram).

The diagram's labels don't match the rest of the paper:

- **Figure caption (page 6):** It says the history tower aggregates recent interaction embeddings "using positional attention," not GeM pooling.
- **Method text (Sections 4.2–4.3, page 5):** The history embedding is computed with position-aware attention (Eq. 5). The final query representation comes from normalized additive fusion of the profile and history embeddings (Eqs. 3–4). The term "temporal-gated pooling" doesn't appear anywhere in the text.
- **Experiments (Tables 1–2, page 7):** GeM pooling is one of the history aggregation methods compared. It scored a MAR@100 of 0.447, just behind P-ATT (positional attention) at 0.450. P-ATT is the variant deployed in the online A/B test (page 8).

The diagram may show an earlier or alternative configuration, but the document doesn't explain the difference.
